channel.title: Noushad Hossain — Writing
channel.description: Engineering notes on PostgreSQL, data pipelines, LLM agents, email infrastructure and running small platforms in production.

item.title: Idempotent batch APIs with an external_id
item.description: Designing a certification platform's provider API so retried batches never duplicate certificates and partners can integrate without talking to us.

item.title: A channel taxonomy in one CSV
item.description: The most useful thing to come out of a dbt spike was fifteen lines of CSV: one place where every vendor's channel name maps to ours.

item.title: A week with dbt Core and its sharp defaults
item.description: A time-boxed spike to decide whether dbt fits our silver-to-gold layer: it did everything asked, and showed how easily it produces silently wrong data.

item.title: Test your row-level security as a non-superuser
item.description: RLS tests that run as the postgres superuser prove nothing. How the Intelect test suite exercises the policies for real, and what that costs.

item.title: Two layers of tenant isolation: ORM hooks and Postgres row-level security
item.description: How a multi-tenant CRM on one shared PostgreSQL database keeps tenants apart twice: once in SQLAlchemy, once in the database itself.

item.title: Migrating a WordPress site to Postgres without running MySQL
item.description: Two education platforms moved from WordPress to FastAPI and Postgres 16. The migration pipeline is reproducible, keeps a safety net, and lets old passwords keep working.

item.title: Secrets hygiene for a small platform
item.description: The written rules InkPigeon follows for passwords, API keys, DKIM keys, logging, configuration and migrations, and why they are rules rather than habits.

item.title: Where port 25 works: hosting an email platform in 2026
item.description: Most cloud providers will not let you send mail on port 25. How that constraint shaped where and how InkPigeon runs.

item.title: Two privilege escalations I shipped, and the rules that came out of it
item.description: InkPigeon's custom-roles feature passed its tests and still had two ways to escalate privileges. What a dedicated adversarial pass found, and the rules it produced.

item.title: The mail queue lives in PostgreSQL
item.description: InkPigeon's delivery workers claim messages with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED instead of a Redis or Celery queue. The reasoning and the trade-off.

item.title: A modular monolith on one VPS
item.description: InkPigeon is one Python codebase deployed as about eight containers that scale independently. Why that beats microservices on a single server.

item.title: Build or adopt: why InkPigeon doesn't run on Mailu or Postal
item.description: I evaluated five open-source mail products before building InkPigeon's own pipeline. Here is what each one is, and why only two components survived.

item.title: AI coding sessions need a standards file
item.description: I use AI coding assistants heavily. The thing that keeps them from drifting is not a better prompt but a written standards file that outranks the model.

item.title: The cutover playbook: swap a base URL, add a pipe, prove it on auth first
item.description: How we move frontend modules from legacy endpoints to a new backend one constructor at a time, and why the first cutover is the one that matters.

item.title: Deleting endpoints safely: a code audit is not enough
item.description: Seven groups of old API endpoints have zero callers in our code. We still are not deleting them until the access logs agree.

item.title: Replacing a five-year rewrite with a bounded migration
item.description: Our plan to migrate all 18 modules to a new architecture would have taken 3.5 to 6 years. Here is how we replaced it with a target the company could actually reach.

item.title: Who owns which layer: Python, dbt and Celery
item.description: Before choosing a transform tool for our ETL v2 platform, we fixed which layer each component owns. The boundaries outlived the tool decision.

item.title: Idempotent ingestion: run IDs, file hashes and row hashes
item.description: How the bronze layer of our ETL v2 design makes every load safe to re-run, and why a data contract has to exist before the first table does.

item.title: A security gate that doesn't block delivery
item.description: How I built our GitHub Actions staging pipeline to fail on security findings by default while letting a reviewer approve a deployment with a record.

item.title: One hotel, five identifiers: reconciling identities across vendor APIs
item.description: Why the hardest problem in a multi-source analytics platform is agreeing on which hotel a row belongs to, and how we made that explicit.

item.title: Grounding LLM reports in your own APIs
item.description: How we added LLM-written narrative reports to an analytics platform without letting the model invent a single number.

item.title: What a coding agent costs per pull request
item.description: Why I built a per-run cost ledger into my coding agent, and how knowing the price of a pull request changed which tickets I give it.

item.title: Four tools are enough: designing a bounded coding-agent loop
item.description: How I built an agent that turns well-specified tickets into pull requests with four tools, hard limits and a provider abstraction.

item.title: Missing data should be a state, not a silence
item.description: How the analytics platform I lead turned silent gaps in vendor data into tracked states with monitors, triggers and automatic resolution.

item.title: Running periodic vendor syncs with Celery beat and a database scheduler
item.description: Why the analytics platform I lead keeps its sync schedules in PostgreSQL rather than in code, and what went wrong before it did.
